question: What does HTML stand for? 🌐
explanation: Brilliant! HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language. It is the standard language used to create and design webpages. 💻
hint: Think about 'Hyper Text' and 'Markup'.

question: Which software is used to view an HTML webpage? 🖥️
explanation: Awesome! Web browsers like Chrome, Firefox, or Edge read the HTML code and display it as a beautiful webpage. 🌐
hint: You use this app to 'surf' the internet.

question: Which of the following is the root element of an HTML document? 🌳
explanation: Great job! The <html> tag is the root element that wraps all the content on the entire page. 📦
hint: It shares its name with the language itself.

question: Where do you write the <title> tag of a webpage? 📌
explanation: Spot on! The <title> tag always goes inside the <head> section, and it shows up on the browser tab. 📑
hint: Think of the 'top' part of the HTML document structure.

question: Which tag contains all the visible content of your webpage, like text, images, and links? 🖼️
explanation: Fantastic! The <body> tag holds everything that a user actually sees on the main screen of the web browser. 📺
hint: It is the main 'torso' of the web page.

question: How many heading levels are available in HTML? 📏
explanation: Perfect! HTML provides six levels of headings, ranging from <h1> to <h6>, to structure your content. 📚
hint: Count from h1, h2, h3... up to what?

question: Which HTML tag displays the largest heading? 🐘
explanation: Excellent! The <h1> tag represents the most important and largest heading on the page. 🏆
hint: Number 1 means top priority and biggest size.

question: Which HTML tag is used to create a paragraph? 📝
explanation:
Well done! The

hint: It is just the first letter of the word 'paragraph'.

question: Which HTML tag is used to insert a single line break? ⌨️
explanation:

hint: It stands for 'break'.

question: Which HTML tag draws a horizontal line across the webpage? ➖
explanation: Superb! The <hr> tag stands for 'horizontal rule' and is used to separate content with a visual line. 📏
hint: Think of 'Horizontal Rule'.

question: Which tag makes your text bold? 💪
explanation: Great catch! Both <b> and <strong> make text appear bold, though <strong> also tells screen readers the text is important. 🗣️
hint: There are two correct tags that do this visually.

question: Which tag makes your text italicized (slanted)? 🤌
explanation: Correct! The <i> tag makes text italic. You can also use the <em> (emphasis) tag for a similar effect! ✨
hint: It is the first letter of 'italic'.

question: Which tag is used to underline text in HTML? 🖍️
explanation: Awesome! The <u> tag underlines the text enclosed within it. Just remember not to confuse it with links! 🔗
hint: It is the first letter of 'underline'.

question: What is the correct file extension when saving an HTML file? 💾
explanation: Perfect! You must save your files with a .html or .htm extension so the computer knows to open it with a web browser. 🌍
hint: It matches the acronym of the language.

question: Who is known as the inventor of HTML? 👨‍🔬
explanation: Spot on! Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented HTML in 1991 while working at CERN. 🚀
hint: He also invented the World Wide Web.

question: Which of these programs can be used as a text editor to write HTML code? ⌨️
explanation: That is right! Simple text editors like Notepad (Windows) or TextEdit (Mac) are great for writing HTML code. 📝
hint: It is a basic app used for taking plain text notes.

question: What provides extra information about an HTML element and is always written in the opening tag? ℹ️
explanation: Brilliant! Attributes give extra instructions to an element, like defining the color or size, and always go in the starting tag. 🛠️
hint: It starts with an 'A' and means a quality or feature.

question: Is HTML a case-sensitive language? 🔠
explanation: Correct! HTML tags can be written in uppercase, lowercase, or a mix. However, writing in lowercase is the standard best practice! 🔡
hint:
Can you write

and

and get the same result?

question: What is the correct way to write the HTML5 document type declaration? 📜
explanation: Excellent! <!DOCTYPE html> tells the web browser that the page is written in HTML5. It always goes at the very top! 🔝
hint: It starts with an exclamation mark (!).

question: Which tag displays the smallest heading in HTML? 🐁
explanation: Awesome! The <h6> tag is the 6th level of headings and it is the smallest heading tag available. 📏
hint: It is the highest number available for an 'h' tag.

question: If you want to write H2O, which tag is used to make the '2' appear slightly below the normal text line? 💧
explanation: Spot on! The <sub> tag creates subscript text, which is perfect for writing chemical formulas like H2O! 🧪
hint: Think of a 'submarine' going down.

question: If you want to write a mathematical formula like x squared (x²), which tag do you use for the '2'? 🧮
explanation: Brilliant! The <sup> tag creates superscript text, floating the text slightly above the normal line. Perfect for math! ✖️
hint: Think of 'Superman' flying up high.

question: What do we call HTML tags that have both an opening tag and a closing tag? 📦
explanation:
That is right! Container elements 'contain' content between their opening and closing tags, like

This is a container!

. 📦
hint: They act like a box holding items inside.

question: What happens if you type lots of extra spaces between words in your HTML code? ⌨️
explanation: Great observation! Web browsers fold multiple spaces into a single space. This is known as 'white space collapsing'. 📏
hint: Browsers are very strict about cleaning up blank areas.

question: Which tag allows you to keep spaces and line breaks exactly as you typed them in the code? 🎹
explanation: Fantastic! The <pre> tag stands for 'preformatted text'. It tells the browser to display spaces and line breaks exactly as written. 🖼️
hint: Short for 'preformatted'.

question: Which tags are properly nested? 🪆
explanation: Perfect! Tags must be closed in the reverse order they were opened. First opened, last closed! 🪆
hint: The inner tag must be closed before the outer tag.

question: What attribute was traditionally used on the <body> tag to change the background color? 🎨
explanation: Correct! While CSS is the modern way, 'bgcolor' is the classic HTML attribute used to change the background color of a page. 🌈
hint: It stands for 'background color' as a single word.

question: Which HTML element visually draws a line to separate sections of a document? 📏
explanation: Awesome! The <hr> tag inserts a thematic break in the form of a horizontal line. 📐
hint: Short for 'Horizontal Rule'.

question: Which tag defines text that has a strike-through line crossing it out? 🚫
explanation: Spot on! Both tags render text with a line through it, though <del> is semantically preferred for 'deleted' text in modern HTML. ✂️
hint: There are two acceptable answers here.

question: Which tag emphasizes text, similar to making it italic? ✨
explanation: Well done! The <em> tag adds semantic emphasis to text, and browsers usually display it in italics. 🌟
hint: It is short for 'emphasis'.

question: Which tag represents the metadata and links to scripts, not seen by the page visitor? 🧠
explanation: Right! The <head> section is like the 'brain' of the document. It holds data about the page but isn't displayed on the screen. 💡
hint: It is the opposite of the body.

question: True or False: The text inside the <title> tags is displayed in the main body of the webpage. 🏷️
explanation: Great catch! The text inside the <title> tag appears on the browser tab or window title bar, not in the main page content. 📑
hint: Look up at the tabs on your browser.

question: What is the function of the <center> tag (historically)? 🎯
explanation: Correct! While modern HTML uses CSS, the <center> tag was used to align text or images to the middle of the screen. 🎯
hint: The name gives it away!

question: Which sequence outlines the basic structure of an HTML document correctly? 🧱
explanation: Fantastic! An HTML document always starts with <html>, has a <head> section, followed by a <body> section, and then closes </html>. 🏗️
hint: Open HTML, do the head, then do the body, close HTML.

question: In the tag <body bgcolor='red'>, what is 'red'? 🔴
explanation: Brilliant! 'red' is the value assigned to the 'bgcolor' attribute. Values are usually wrapped in quotes. 🎨
hint: It is what the attribute is equal to.

hint: Which one of these holds text and needs to be closed?

question: What do we use to wrap attribute values in HTML? 🎁
explanation: Correct! Attribute values should always be enclosed in quotation marks, like bgcolor="blue". 📝
hint: They look like speech marks.

question: What is the correct tag for creating a large bold text to act as the main title of a news article? 📰
explanation: Great job! The <h1> tag is semantic and structural, meant to be the main heading on the visible page. 🏆
hint: It's the highest level heading.

question: Which tag would you use to define a secondary heading, slightly smaller than the main heading? 🥈
explanation: Perfect! The <h2> tag is used for subheadings immediately under an <h1> heading. 📉
hint: It is the number right after 1.

question: Can you use multiple <h1> tags on a single webpage? 📑
options: Yes, but it is better to use only one for the main title ✅
answer: Yes, but it is better to use only one for the main title ✅
explanation: Spot on! While code-wise it works, standard SEO and structural practice suggests having just one <h1> per page for the main topic. 🥇
hint: It is not forbidden, but it's like having multiple book titles.

question: Which of these is a correctly formatted HTML comment? 🤫
explanation: Excellent! HTML comments start with <!-- and end with -->. Browsers hide these from the users! 👻
hint: It uses an exclamation mark and dashes.

question: What does a web browser do with an HTML file? 🖥️
options: Reads the tags and translates them into a visual page 🎨
Sends it back to the server 📤
answer: Reads the tags and translates them into a visual page 🎨
explanation: Awesome! A browser parses the HTML markup and renders it so that humans can see a beautiful web page instead of raw code. 🌍
hint: It acts like a translator for web code.

question: Which tag makes the text smaller than the surrounding regular text? 🔬
explanation: That is right! The <small> tag shrinks the text size down by one level compared to the regular text size. 🔎
hint: The opposite of big.

question: Which tag makes the text larger than the surrounding regular text? 🔎
explanation: Great answer! The <big> tag makes the enclosed text stand out by making it larger than standard text. 📈
hint: The opposite of small.

question: If you forget to put a closing slash in a container tag, what might happen? ⚠️
options: The effect continues to the rest of the page 🌊
answer: The effect continues to the rest of the page 🌊
explanation: Good thinking! If you forget to close a tag like <b>, the browser keeps making everything bold until the end of the page! 🏃‍♂️
hint: The browser doesn't know where to stop.

question: What is 'HTML' categorized as? 🗂️
explanation: Perfect! HTML is a 'Markup' language, which means it uses tags to annotate or structure text. It is not a programming language like Python or C++. 🧱
hint: Look at the 'M' in HTML.

question: Where does the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration go in your HTML file? 🔝
explanation: Exactly! It must be the very first line of code to tell the browser what version of HTML to expect before reading anything else. 🚀
hint: It leads the entire document.

question: Which of these tags is essential for search engines to know the name of your webpage? 🔍
explanation: Spot on! Search engines use the <title> tag found in the <head> to display your webpage's name in search results! 🌐
hint: It's the name that appears on the browser tab.
